title: Double rotation: left-right
summary: When the extra height is on the inside, one rotation is not enough. Two rotations fix it.

checkpoints.text: 25 went left of 50, then right of 20, then left of 30. Back at 50, the left side is now 3 levels tall and the right side 1: a balance of +2.

The extra height is in 20's right side: a zig-zag (left, then right). A single right rotation at 50 would just move the zig-zag to the other side. First, a left rotation at 20 straightens it into a line.
Now the right rotation at 50. The first rotation changed who is directly below 50 on the left.
30 was lifted twice and is now on top, with 20 and 50 as its children; 25 was handed to 20. `insert` returns 30, so `root` in `main` will point at it.
Pre-order 30 20 10 25 50 70: every node is balanced again. The rotation and insert functions are the ones from the Lab 9 manual, written outside a class, with `max()` working as in real C++.
